name: Tiger-Tribe Hunter
oracle_text:
Trample
Pack tactics — Whenever this creature attacks, if you attacked with creatures with total power 6 or greater this combat, you may sacrifice another creature. When you do, this creature deals damage equal to the sacrificed creature's power to target creature.
blocked_sentences: Pack tactics — Whenever this creature attacks, if you attacked with creatures with total power 6 or greater this combat, you may sacrifice another creature. When you do, this creature deals damage equal to the sacrificed creature's power to target creature.

needs.what: `may` with `pay: {sacrifice: {..., as: name}}` writing the sacrificed creature's snapshot into the effect bindings, so a reflexive_trigger in its effects can read `power_of {binding: name}` -- "you may sacrifice another creature. When you do, ... the sacrificed creature's power"
needs.why_existing_wont_do: op_may pays its cost without a bindings dict, so a cost's `as` names nothing there. Writing the sacrifice as an effect op inside may instead fires the reflexive trigger even when nothing could be sacrificed (a creature under a can't-be-sacrificed effect), which the printed 'When you do' does not. The pack tactics condition itself is attack_power_this_combat
